text:
sam: Heads-up — prod gpu-provisioner is spiking Pending pods. model-fetch logs show DNS failures for our internal service records (NXDOMAIN / truncated responses). throwing autoscaler off :confused:

maya: ugh. any immediate error lines? which fqdn?

sam: internal-svc.mesh.prod.cluster.local and a couple of SRV lookups for _model._tcp.internal-svc. errors look like: 'status: NXDOMAIN' then sometimes 'connection timed out' in libcurl. here's the resolv.conf on a repro node:

```
# /etc/resolv.conf (container)
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options edns0 single-request-reopen
search prod.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
ndots:5
```

sam: tcpdump showed a lot of UDP 512+ truncated (TC=1) responses and then fallback to TCP which never completed. sample tcpdump line: `IP 10.1.3.5.53 > 10.2.4.7.33333: UDP, length 512, Flags [none], TC`

jordan: if TC=1 that means truncated UDP. usually DNS should fall back to TCP. are outbound TCP/53 connections blocked on the NAT/egress?

sam: thats what i suspected. i ran `dig +dnssec @10.10.10.5 _model._tcp.internal-svc.svc.cluster.local SRV +tcp` and the TCP query hung. UDP returned Truncated.

eli: ran an egress trace from edge-nat gw:

```
# from edge-nat
$ sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53
12:03:01.123456 IP 10.10.10.5.35678 > 8.8.8.8.53: UDP, length 512
12:03:01.123489 IP 8.8.8.8.53 > 10.10.10.5.35678: UDP, length 1230 (frag?) TC
12:03:01.123700 IP 10.10:10.5.35679 > 8.8.8.8.53: Flags [S], seq 0
12:03:01.124000 IP 8.8.8.8.53 > 10.10.10.5.35679: RST
```

eli: looks like UDP replies are big (EDNS0) so truncated, client tries TCP but our NAT/firewall is resetting the TCP 53 handshake. i grep'd iptables and saw a rule disallowing outbound tcp dport 53 in the older policy (left over from a compliance lockdown).

maya: wow. why would our internal forwarder be using EDNS0 large replies? some SRV records + TXT metadata push it over 512 bytes. we do have large TXT blobs for model metadata.

sam: right. until now most recursors handled it fine. but the new forwarder pair in eu-west added DNSSEC + longer responses.

infra-bot: [alert] gpu-provisioner: service "model-fetch" error rate 34% over 5m — routing to fallback pool

jordan: mitigation options: 1) allow outbound TCP/53 on NAT/firewall (best), 2) reduce EDNS size on forwarders to force smaller UDP replies (workaround), 3) strip large TXT fields at the source (hard).

eli: quick check command to see firewall block: `sudo hping3 -S -p 53 8.8.8.8` (SYN) — if it gets RST then firewall actively rejecting. we also confirmed conntrack ephemeral port exhaustion in one NAT cluster during the spike.

sam: for immediate relief i'm going to open egress TCP/53 on the affected NATs and bump conntrack timeouts. applying as patch to the terraform firewall rules for prod-egress. rolling change in 5m.

maya: please post the terraform diff here when you have it. also add a short-lived monitor for tcp/53 handshake success on the forwarders.

sam: terraform diff:
```
resource "cloud_fw_rule" "allow_dns_tcp" {
  name = "allow-egress-dns-tcp"
  direction = "egress"
  protocol = "tcp"
  ports = [53]
  cidr_blocks = ["10.10.10.0/24", "10.11.0.0/16"]
  description = "Allow outbound tcp/53 for DNS fallback for large replies"
}
```

sam: rolling to NATs now. will ping when done. :rocket:

(15m later)

sam: change applied. tcp 53 handshakes now complete, dig +tcp returns full SRV records and TXT. provisioner errors dropping to 1.2%

eli: added a short Prom rule on the egress NATs: `probe_dns_tcp_success` (attempts tcp handshake to upstreams every 30s). alert if <95% over 5m.

jordan: we'll also schedule a follow-up to evaluate trimming TXT sizes and/or serving model metadata from a separate smaller record to avoid hitting EDNS/UDP limits.

maya: thanks all — good catch. leaving incident open for postmortem and action items (firewall rule template, conntrack tuning, doc update for DNS/EDNS pitfalls). :thumbsup:
